Subject: Tenant fiber demarc & control/data interop — initial ask

Hi Mateo,

Thanks again for the walkthrough last week. The networking team at Aurora asked me to loop you in with a concrete ask: before we lock down the colo cutover we need a short design review that validates how Redwood's control plane and data plane will traverse the tenant fiber demarc at our site. Key questions:

- Which side initiates TLS for mTLS handshakes (Aurora edge vs Redwood control plane)?
- How will KV cache traffic be routed across the demarc when we have both local on-prem inference nodes and cross-site fallback?
- Any minimum MTU/IP fragmentation considerations for the jumbo frames we plan to enable?

I've attached a rough demarc sketch (aurora-proposed-demarc.svg) and a short appendix of requirements. Can your team do a 45-minute review next week (Aug 1 preferred)? We also want explicit fallthrough behavior described for the control plane in outage modes.

Ellen
Ellen Price
Sr. Infrastructure Program Manager, Aurora Cloud

On Thu, Jul 25, 2029 at 10:03 AM Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.com> wrote:
> Folks — forwarding Aurora's ask.

Quick notes from the control-plane side (first pass):

- mTLS initiation: Redwood's control-plane agent initiates the connection to the control endpoint (we terminate on our control-edge). For private deployments we can support either direction, but the current agent defaults to outbound TLS from the customer network to the control-plane endpoint. If Aurora requires inbound termination, we'll need a secure reverse-proxy/handshake gateway at the demarc (adds NAT and port mapping complexity).

- Certificate trust: recommend a short-lived cert rotation window (7–14 days) for the agent identity certs; Aurora's ops will need CA chain push access (or we use a mutual CA-signed cert distribution).

- Failure modes:
  1) Control-plane loss: agents should enter local-only mode and switch to a configured fallback model version pinned for offline inference. We'll produce explicit runbook steps.
  2) Partial path with asymmetric routing: tag control-plane traffic with DSCP and rely on Aurora's ACLs to preserve flow symmetry during failover.

Risks / asks:
- Confirm whether Aurora will accept outbound-only control plane connections from customer VLANs. If not, we'll scope a proxy gateway design.
- Need MTU confirmation (see Jonas for data-plane impact).

I'll draft a 1-page control-plane handshake sequence and share by Jul 31.

—Naomi
Naomi Feldman
Principal Network Engineer, Redwood Inference
